issues.description: IAM policy fetch failure is silently coerced to publicly_shared=False, producing a false PASS
issues.detail: In _get_images(), when getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied as exercised by test-image-3, transient API error, throttling), the code logs the error and falls through with publicly_shared=False. The image is appended and the check emits PASS — asserting 'this image is not publicly shared' for an image whose policy could not be read. This is the worst failure mode for a security scanner: a green light because we could not see. Either skip the image on fetch failure, or introduce a tri-state (Optional[bool] / iam_policy_retrieved flag / explicit unknown) and surface MANUAL/ERROR rather than PASS. The current test for test-image-3 codifies this unsafe default and must change alongside the fix.

issues.description: Check name disagrees across CHANGELOG/code (compute_image_not_publicly_shared) vs. PR description (compute_image_publicly_shared)
issues.detail: The CHANGELOG entry, directory, class, and metadata all use `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`, but the PR title and description repeatedly reference `compute_image_publicly_shared`. The identifier is the contract: it flows through tooling, dashboards, and remediation links, and the artifact currently disagrees with itself. Pick one canonical name and propagate it everywhere a reader will look (PR body, CHANGELOG, code, metadata, docs). Also reconcile positive-vs-negative naming convention for the GCP check family so CheckID semantics (PASS-asserts vs. violation-names) are predictable.

issues.description: Image model is anemic: stores only a derived boolean instead of public_members / bindings
issues.detail: The service layer reduces the IAM policy to a single boolean before the check ever sees it, discarding which members and roles were granted. The PR description itself claims the model carries `public_members`, but the actual model only has name/id/project_id/publicly_shared. This loses the data a remediator needs (which principal? which role?) and prevents future checks from reasoning about role-specific exposure without re-fetching. Store the raw bindings or at minimum `public_members: list[str]` on Image; let the check derive the boolean and present the offending members in status_extended. Data dominates: store the fact, derive the predicate.

issues.description: Service test for image-3 pins the unsafe silent-PASS behavior in place
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py asserts `not compute_client.images[2].publicly_shared` for the image whose getIamPolicy raises 'Permission denied'. This codifies the weakened postcondition (unknown == not-public). When the tri-state / skip fix lands, this assertion must be rewritten to assert unknown/skip semantics. Flagged so the fix and the test move together rather than the test blocking the fix.

issues.description: Check tests round-trip a mocked boolean instead of exercising the binding-to-FAIL path end-to-end
issues.detail: The check tests construct `Image(publicly_shared=True/False)` directly and assert the check echoes the boolean back. There is no test that drives a real IAM binding containing allAuthenticatedUsers through `_get_images` to a FAIL finding. The interesting logic — IAM extraction, the swallowed-exception path, pagination — is never wired to a check finding. Add at least one integration-style test where the check runs against an Image whose bindings/public_members contain allAuthenticatedUsers and the check derives FAIL itself.

issues.description: _get_images runs serially while sibling collectors use __threading_call__
issues.detail: Every other late-stage collector in __init__ parallelizes across regions/zones/projects via `self.__threading_call__(...)`. `_get_images` is invoked once, synchronously, and inside it issues one getIamPolicy per image per project sequentially. For accounts with many projects/images this is a substantial latency cliff and breaks the implicit pattern callers expect. Either thread per project_id like the disk/MIG collectors, or document why images stay serial. Decomposing collection from IAM resolution also makes time/IO explicit instead of hidden in a nested loop.

issues.description: error.__traceback__.tb_lineno dereference can itself raise AttributeError
issues.detail: Both log sites format `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno`. If __traceback__ is None (re-raised exceptions, certain mock paths), this dereference throws inside the except handler, producing an uglier failure than the original. The pattern matches existing house style in compute_service.py, but the PR duplicates the footgun in another place. A small `_log_gcp_error(...)` helper or a None-check would make it safe and shrink call sites.

synthesis.summary: The check is small and the happy-path algorithm is correct, but the contract around it has one fix-or-die issue and several shape problems. The blocking issue: `_get_images` silently coerces getIamPolicy failures to `publicly_shared=False` and the check emits PASS — a security scanner returning green on access denied, with tests that pin the unsafe default in place. The shape issue: the Image model collapses the IAM policy to a derived boolean, losing the public_members/roles a remediator needs and making an unknown state unrepresentable; policy interpretation belongs in the check, not the service. Naming disagrees across CHANGELOG/code (`compute_image_not_publicly_shared`) and PR description (`compute_image_publicly_shared`) and must be reconciled. Secondary: the collector runs serially while sibling collectors parallelize via `__threading_call__`, the check tests only round-trip a mocked boolean rather than exercise binding-to-FAIL, and `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno` is a latent dereference footgun. NEEDS-WORK before merge.
